review_scope: Independent read-only review of isolated profile-only raw-Parquet hash/page-cache advice code. This does not admit packetization, provider execution, fit, scoring, or any scientific claim.

findings.detail: Diff against the frozen v2 worker is limited to a new candidate packet ID, optional hash-advice helper/receipt, use of that helper for raw train/valid parquet SHA-256, and inclusion of its receipt in successful profile output. Expected SHA-256 values, byte counts, footer checks, assets, split/membership checks, profile recipe, and resource caps remain unchanged.

The helper updates SHA-256 with the same sequential bytes in order. A bounded local synthetic file of 3 MiB + 4 bytes, hashed using the real os.posix_fadvise implementation, matched hashlib's reference digest; it made three aligned advice calls and recorded the complete digest. The existing synthetic suite also passed byte-equivalence and page-alignment checks.

On the Linux target, POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED on page-aligned ranges after each 1 MiB read is an applicable advisory for clean file-backed page-cache pages. The code rounds the advised end down to the system page size, checks block/page compatibility, and leaves at most the final partial page unadvised. A successful call is only a hint; it does not prove that pages were reclaimed.

Unavailable advice support fails before reading. Advice/read errors write a durable failed progress record and abort without an unadvised fallback. Byte-count drift aborts. On completed hashes, expected and observed raw-Parquet identity data are persisted before mismatch comparison, preserving the v2 fail-closed identity check. The existing strict resource gates remain unchanged.
No model, fit, prediction, evaluation, data-membership, or score path changed. The candidate remains profile-only.

actual_local_posix_fadvise_probe.scope: small temporary file only; no mounted dataset, GPU, packet, provider, fit, or scoring

verification.resource_boundary: All Python checks were run through scripts/limited at 1 CPU, 1.5 GB memory, and 120 seconds maximum.

non_blocking_diagnostic_recommendation: For the next admitted profile attempt, capture a small cgroup-v2 memory.stat sample (at least file, inactive_file, active_file, file_dirty, file_writeback) alongside existing memory.current/headroom snapshots before and after raw parquet hashing. This would test whether file cache caused the prior headroom abort and whether advice reduced it; successful fadvise calls alone cannot establish eviction. The missing sample does not block this code review because the candidate labels the diagnosis as an inference and retains strict abort gates.
limitations: No Kaggle or mounted-parquet execution was performed; actual cgroup cache response remains unmeasured.
This PASS is for the isolated profile-worker code only and does not admit packetization, cloud execution, fitting, or scoring.
